paper_title: TL;DR Too Long, Do Re-weighting for Effcient LLM Reasoning Compression
caption: Comparison of accuracy and generation length between Vanilla CoT and our method on four benchmark datasets (GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, AMC) using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models. consistently reduces generation length while maintaining or improving accuracy across both 7B and 14B model scales.

model_annotations.English: The bar chart titled "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B Generation Length Comparison" visually compares the generation length (in words) of two reasoning methods—Vanilla CoT (light pink bars) and TLDR (Ours, dark red bars)—across four benchmark datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and AMC. The vertical axis represents generation length in words, scaled linearly from 0 to 8000 with major tick marks at intervals of 1000. The horizontal axis lists the four datasets in left-to-right order without any specific sorting criteria. For each dataset, two adjacent vertical bars are presented: the light pink bar corresponds to Vanilla CoT, and the dark red bar corresponds to TLDR (Ours). The chart shows that TLDR consistently reduces generation length compared to Vanilla CoT across all datasets. On GSM8K, Vanilla CoT generates 554 words, while TLDR reduces it to approximately 255 words (a -54% reduction). On MATH500, Vanilla CoT produces 2861 words, reduced to 1540 words by TLDR (-46%). On AIME, the reduction is from 6820 words (Vanilla CoT) to 6330 words (TLDR), a -7% decrease. On AMC, generation length drops from 4510 words (Vanilla CoT) to 3380 words (TLDR), representing a -25% reduction. Percent reductions are explicitly labeled above each TLDR bar. The bars are arranged in groups by dataset, and there is no visual emphasis or annotation beyond the percentage labels.

For each dataset, two bars are shown side-by-side, with the legend indicating that light pink corresponds to Vanilla CoT and dark red to TLDR (Ours). The chart demonstrates that TLDR consistently reduces generation length compared to Vanilla CoT: on GSM8K, generation length drops from 554 to 254 words (a -54% reduction); on MATH500, from 2861 to 1542 words (-46%); on AIME, from 6820 to 6330 words (-7%); and on AMC, from 4510 to 3380 words (-25%). Percent reductions are explicitly labeled above each dark red bar. The bars are not sorted by length but are grouped by dataset, and no visual emphasis (e.g., shading or annotations) is applied beyond the percentage labels. The data illustrates that TLDR significantly shortens output length across all datasets while maintaining or improving accuracy, as noted in the paper’s caption.
